name: deskyard
description: Use a Deskyard environment (a Linux desktop with a shared Chromium) from inside it or remotely through its server's API, after `deskyard login`. Run commands as `deskyard [-e ENV] <name> <arguments...>`: the global -e ENV or -e SERVER/ENV (--environment) chooses the environment and goes before the command name; arguments are positional in the listed order, and a command's flags go after its name (so exec -e K=V sets an environment variable).

globalFlags.name: --environment
globalFlags.description: the environment to use: ENV on the default server, or SERVER/ENV (see `deskyard server list`); only before the command name: after it, as in `exec -e K=V`, -e is a command's own flag

environment.name: DESKYARD_ENVIRONMENT
environment.description: environment to use when -e isn't given (ENV or SERVER/ENV)

environment.name: DESKYARD_URL
environment.description: server URL, optionally with an environment (https://host/alice), to use instead of the default server; needs DESKYARD_CREDENTIAL

environment.name: DESKYARD_SETTLE
environment.description: seconds screenshot and zoom wait before capturing (default 0.3)

exitCodes.meaning: error (the message on stderr says what to do next)
usage error (bad command, flag or argument)
exec, shell and screen actions pass through the exit code of the command in the environment

commands.name: screenshot
commands.description: Takes a PNG screenshot of the whole screen, after a short settle delay (DESKYARD_SETTLE seconds, default 0.3) so the screen reflects your last action. Without FILE, or with -, the PNG goes to stdout. Take one before acting and after, to see what happened; coordinates in the image are screen coordinates.

arguments.name: file
arguments.description: where to write the PNG on this machine; - or omitted for stdout

output.description: PNG image bytes on stdout, or nothing when FILE is given (the file is written on this machine)

commands.where: inside an environment it acts locally; elsewhere on the chosen environment (-e ENV)
commands.exitCodes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage error; otherwise the exit code of the action on the desktop

commands.name: zoom
commands.summary: PNG of a region at full resolution
commands.description: Takes a PNG of just the region from the top-left corner X0 Y0 to the bottom-right corner X1 Y1 (exclusive), at full resolution: use it to read small text or check details. X1 must be greater than X0 and Y1 greater than Y0.

arguments.name: file

commands.name: exec
commands.summary: run a command in the environment
commands.description: Runs one command as user (in /workspace unless --cwd) and streams its stdin, stdout and stderr; exits with the command's exit code. The command is run as given, not through a shell: for pipes, globs or && use `-- bash -lc '...'`.

flags.name: --json
flags.description: buffer the output and print one JSON object {"stdout","stderr","exit"} instead of streaming; exit 0 when the JSON was printed

flags.name: --tty
flags.description: run in a terminal (for programs that need one); stdout and stderr are merged

flags.name: --env
flags.description: after exec: set an environment variable for the command (repeatable); not the global -e ENV before exec, which chooses the environment

output.description: the command's stdout and stderr as they arrive; with --json one object {"stdout":string,"stderr":string,"exit":int}, using "stdoutBase64"/"stderrBase64" (base64) instead when the output isn't UTF-8

fields.stderrBase64: standard error, base64, when not UTF-8
fields.stdoutBase64: standard output, base64, when not UTF-8

examples: deskyard -e alice exec -e CI=1 -- make test
deskyard exec --json -- bash -lc 'cd app && npm test'
commands.where: on the chosen environment (-e ENV); inside an environment without one chosen it acts locally
commands.exitCodes: the command's own exit code; 1 when it couldn't run (connection, credential, stopped environment), 2 usage error

commands.name: terminal
commands.description: Joins a shared Bash login shell in /workspace, default main. Browser, CLI and desktop clients share the same session. Inside an existing native shared terminal, press Ctrl-B then s and choose the session instead of nesting this command. Detach with Ctrl-B then D; jobs survive disconnect but end when the environment restarts. Session names use 1–64 letters, digits, underscores or dashes and start with a letter or digit.
commands.where: on the chosen environment (-e ENV); inside an environment without one chosen it acts locally
commands.exitCodes: the command's own exit code; 1 when it couldn't run (connection, credential, stopped environment), 2 usage error

commands.name: shell
commands.description: Opens an interactive bash login shell in the environment in your terminal (raw mode, resizes follow your window). Exit with `exit` or Ctrl-D. For scripted use, prefer exec.
commands.where: on the chosen environment (-e ENV); inside an environment without one chosen it acts locally
commands.exitCodes: the shell's exit code; 1 when it couldn't start

commands.name: cp
commands.summary: copy files to or from an environment
commands.description: Copies a file or directory between this machine and an environment; write the environment side as ENV:/path (ENV is an environment on the chosen server, -e SERVER/… or the default one; an empty ENV, as in :/path, means the chosen environment). A file lands at DST, or inside DST when it is an existing directory. A directory's contents land in DST, which is created (like `cp -r SRC/. DST`). SRC - reads stdin; DST - writes to stdout (a tar stream for a directory). Files land as user; inside an environment, two local paths are copied locally.

output.description: nothing, unless DST is - (the file's bytes or a tar stream)

commands.where: on the chosen environment (-e ENV); inside an environment without one chosen it acts locally
commands.exitCodes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage error

commands.name: forward
commands.summary: map TCP ports between this machine and the environment
commands.description: Maps TCP ports both ways until Ctrl-C, over the remote access API (no port is opened anywhere else). Each argument is one mapping. PORT or LOCAL:ENV: this machine's 127.0.0.1:LOCAL becomes localhost:ENV in the environment (a dev server here, reachable by the environment's browser). -R PORT or -R ENV:LOCAL (reverse; one -R before each such mapping): the environment's localhost:ENV becomes 127.0.0.1:LOCAL here. Both ends listen on loopback only; the environment won't listen below 1024 (plain forward only; -R just dials, so -R 80:8080 works). A port in use on either side fails that mapping, which is retried, and the others carry on. When the connection drops (the environment stops or restarts, the network blips) it keeps its local listeners, closes open connections and reconnects with backoff (1 s up to 30 s). It exits only on Ctrl-C, or when the credential is refused. Run it in the background. Inside an environment it needs -e too.

arguments.name: port
arguments.description: a mapping: PORT or LOCAL:ENV; after -R, PORT or ENV:LOCAL

flags.name: --reverse
flags.description: the next mapping is reverse: a port in the environment becomes a port here

output.description: one line per mapping each time it goes live: "in LOCAL ENV" or "out ENV 127.0.0.1:LOCAL"; on stderr one line per state change (linked, lost and retrying, port in use)

fields.in: LOCAL ENV: this machine's port, reachable in the environment at localhost:ENV
fields.out: ENV ADDR: the environment's port, reachable here at ADDR

commands.where: on the chosen environment (-e ENV); inside an environment too, since it maps ports between two machines. Ports are LOCAL:ENV, or ENV:LOCAL after -R. The environment won't listen below 1024. "Linked to ..." and the out lines appear when the link is accepted, before the environment side is known to run
commands.exitCodes: 0 after Ctrl-C, 1 when the credential is refused (401) or no environment is chosen, 2 usage error

commands.name: browser connect
commands.summary: forward the environment's browser to a local CDP port
commands.description: Listens on 127.0.0.1:PORT and forwards the Chrome DevTools Protocol to the environment's shared Chromium (the one on its desktop, with your signed-in sessions), so Playwright, Puppeteer or DevTools tools connect as if the browser were local. Prints the URL, then keeps running until Ctrl-C. Run it in the background. Inside an environment it isn't needed: CDP is at http://127.0.0.1:9221.

output.description: first line: the local CDP URL (http://127.0.0.1:9222); connection log on stderr

commands.where: on the chosen environment (-e ENV); inside an environment without one chosen it acts locally
commands.exitCodes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage error

commands.name: login
commands.summary: sign in to a server, approving in the browser
commands.description: Signs this CLI in to a Deskyard server: prints a code and an approval URL (on stderr) and opens it in your browser, where you check the code and approve while signed in to Deskyard. Then saves the server, your username and a client credential for this machine in servers.json ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/deskyard, default ~/.config/deskyard; mode 0600). With an environment in the URL (https://host/alice) it becomes the server's default environment, once checked that you have full access to it; without one, your only environment does. The first server becomes the default. The request expires after 10 minutes.

arguments.name: url
arguments.description: the server's address, optionally with an environment: https://host or https://host/alice

flags.name: --name
flags.description: local name for the server, used with -e NAME/ENV (default: its host name)

flags.name: --no-browser
flags.description: only print the approval URL, don't open a browser

output.description: a confirmation with the account and environment; the code and approval URL on stderr

commands.where: on this machine, talking to the server
commands.exitCodes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage error

commands.name: auth
commands.summary: sign in to a server with a login link
commands.description: Signs this CLI in with a login link (https://host/link#dyl_…), without a browser: the link is used up, and the server, your username and a client credential are saved in servers.json as for login. When the account has exactly one environment it becomes the default. Observe-only links work in a browser only.

flags.name: --name
flags.description: local name for the server, used with -e NAME/ENV (default: its host name)

output.description: a confirmation with the account and environment

commands.where: on this machine, talking to the server
commands.exitCodes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage error

commands.description: Revokes this CLI's credential on the server (default: the default server), then forgets the server. A credential the server already refuses is forgotten too; when the server can't be reached, nothing is forgotten.
commands.where: on this machine, talking to the server
